# Spec: what this code guarantees

10 rules in force. A person approved each one, and each has a test that must keep passing. This document is generated from the SeamSpec ledger: it lists what was approved, and nothing else.

## Rules in force

### `swerepo` (8 rules)

#### A fingerprint ignores only line endings, trailing whitespace, trailing blank lines and a BOM

A file's fingerprint stays the same when only its line endings (CRLF or CR), trailing whitespace on any line, trailing blank lines, a missing final newline or a leading byte-order mark differ, for text and bytes alike, and changes for any other edit, including indentation, tabs for spaces, and blank or deleted lines inside the text.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/fingerprint.py`
- **Approved by:** Vamshidhar Pandrapagada, 2026-11-20, in the terminal
- **Test:** `.seamspec/tests/test_inv_7c5f3156.py` (pytest)
- **Critical:** always shown to the agent in full
- **Id:** `inv_7c5f3156`

#### Detection never writes to the repository it looks at, with or without git

Running detection leaves every file and folder unchanged (names, sizes and modification times): in a committed git repository whose index is out of date, and in a folder that isn't a repository, while it reads workflows, pre-commit, setup.cfg and tox.ini (and the test checks it found them).

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/detect.py`
- **Approved by:** Vamshidhar Pandrapagada, 2026-11-20, in the terminal
- **Test:** `.seamspec/tests/test_inv_bee7349a.py` (pytest)
- **Critical:** always shown to the agent in full
- **Id:** `inv_bee7349a`

#### An older SWERepo never replaces a .swerepo.toml from a newer SWERepo or standard, loaded, new or stale

An older SWERepo never replaces a .swerepo.toml written by a newer SWERepo version or in a newer standard: not after loading it (it still loads, even naming components this version doesn't know), not with a new state, and not with a state loaded before the newer SWERepo rewrote the file. The file stays unchanged.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/state.py`
- **Approved by:** Vamshidhar Pandrapagada, 2026-11-20, in the terminal
- **Test:** `.seamspec/tests/test_inv_71e4b33d.py` (pytest)
- **Critical:** always shown to the agent in full
- **Replaces:** A .swerepo.toml from a newer SWERepo or standard loads, but an older SWERepo never overwrites it (`inv_070db19c`)
- **Id:** `inv_71e4b33d`

#### Saving .swerepo.toml keeps comments and unknown keys, also inside records SWERepo updates

Saving .swerepo.toml, including after SWERepo changed values and updated or added records, and when a newer SWERepo saves, keeps comments on their own line and at the end of lines it changed, and every key SWERepo doesn't know (top-level, in a table it knows, in a record it updated, or in a table of its own) with its value.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/state.py`
- **Approved by:** Vamshidhar Pandrapagada, 2026-11-20, in the terminal
- **Test:** `.seamspec/tests/test_inv_afb6dfea.py` (pytest)
- **Replaces:** Saving .swerepo.toml, also after changes, keeps people's comments and every key SWERepo doesn't know (`inv_d8603926`)
- **Id:** `inv_afb6dfea`

#### Check never writes to the folder it checks, not even git's index

Running `swerepo check` leaves every file and folder unchanged (names, sizes, modification times and contents, git's index included): in a git repository whose index is out of date, with all six default components, a file recorded in .swerepo.toml, the pull-request rules (`--base`) and the command line (`--base --ci` on GitHub Actions, with and without `--json`); and in a folder that isn't a git repository. The test confirms each part ran: a finding from each of the six components and the recorded file, the new dependency found by the diff, and both command-line runs finishing with exit code 1, annotations and parsable JSON.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/check.py`, `swerepo/prrules.py`, `swerepo/cli.py`, `swerepo/state.py`, `swerepo/detect.py`

#### Check output shows no absolute paths or personal emails, in the cases tested

In a repository where git's configured email and a commit use a personal address, a CODEOWNERS line after SWERepo's block is just that address, and .swerepo.toml can't be read (the error names its absolute path), `swerepo check` output in text, `--json`, and `--ci` annotations on GitHub Actions, each with the pull-request rules (`--base`), contains neither the address nor the checked folder's absolute path (as given or resolved), its parent's, or the home folder. The test confirms each case's message (unreadable state file, configured email, commit email, CODEOWNERS, missing progress entry) appears in every output.

#### init never replaces or edits a file it didn't write, except adding its block at the end

`swerepo init` keeps every existing file's text byte for byte: in a repository with its own README, AGENTS.md (CRLF, ending in two blank lines), CLAUDE.md (no final newline), CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, PROGRESS and an ADR of its own, each file is either unchanged, or is its whole original text (blank lines at its end included) followed only by the line breaks that make one blank line and a single SWERepo marked block that ends the file, in the file's own line endings. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both gain a block, and the ADR index init creates lists the person's ADR. After a person edits SWERepo's AGENTS.md block and a runbook it wrote, the next `init` leaves both as the person left them. A file or a SWERepo block that appears between the plan and applying it stops init with an error and nothing written: no file replaced, no block doubled, no other file or block added.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/init.py`, `swerepo/blocks.py`, `swerepo/adr.py`, `swerepo/cli.py`
- **Approved by:** Vamshidhar Pandrapagada, 2026-11-22, in the terminal
- **Test:** `.seamspec/tests/test_inv_8314036c.py` (pytest)
- **Critical:** always shown to the agent in full
- **Id:** `inv_8314036c`

#### init --dry-run writes nothing, and a second init on a set-up repository writes nothing

In a git repository with a pyproject.toml and its own CLAUDE.md, `swerepo init --dry-run` exits 0, prints a plan with something to create, and leaves every file and folder unchanged (names, sizes, modification times and contents, `.git` included). After `swerepo init --yes` has applied it, a second `swerepo init --yes` exits 0, says "Nothing to do." and again leaves everything unchanged.

- **Applies to:** `swerepo/init.py`, `swerepo/blocks.py`, `swerepo/adr.py`, `swerepo/cli.py`, `swerepo/state.py`

### `(repository root)` (2 rules)

#### No personal email addresses or home-folder paths in tracked files

Every tracked text file is free of personal email addresses and home-folder paths. Allowed: GitHub noreply addresses, reserved example domains, git@ in SSH remotes, emails declared in pyproject.toml's [project] authors and maintainers, emails in SECURITY.md, placeholder home folders (/Users/me, /home/user, C:\Users\you, runner, Shared), and any line marked 'swerepo: allow-privacy'.

## Tried and failed

Approaches that were tried and did not work. They carry no test; they are here so nobody repeats them without knowing why they failed.

### `swerepo`

- **Tried:** Keep `git diff <ref>` (working tree against a commit) from writing .git/index by adding `git --no-optional-locks`.
  - **Why it failed:** With an out-of-date index (a file touched but unchanged), `git --no-optional-locks diff --name-status <ref>` still rewrote .git/index (mtime changed; git 2.50). The switch does not cover `git diff`. Fix used: run that diff with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at a temporary copy of the index. Plain `git diff-index` without refreshing doesn't write but reports touched-but-unchanged files as modified.
  - Applies to `swerepo/check.py`, `swerepo/prrules.py`, `swerepo/detect.py` · recorded 2026-11-21 · `de_a22b43fe`
